subject: CareLab: Request for non-training proof and subprocessor export plan
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@carelab.health>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: CareLab Security Team <security@carelab.health>
Date: 2028-04-25T09:13:00Z
Subject: Evidence of non-training (CareLab production data) + subprocessor export path

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our procurement checklist we need two things before we can finalize the pilot SOW:

1) Concrete, operational evidence that CareLab production inputs will not be used to further train or evaluate any public or internal models ("no-training"): what artifacts can Redwood provide (logs, retention policies, KMS attestations, and an ops runbook showing enforced exclusions)?

2) A subprocessor export plan: if any telemetry or artifacts are transferred for debugging or infra purposes, show the route(s), country residency, and a fallback to onshore EU processing.

We tried to capture this in the attached DPA redline but wanted the operational proof in parallel. Can you share a single evidence package we can send to procurement/security? Also flag anything time-sensitive — procurement will close the loop by 05/05.

Best,
Asha
Director, Infrastructure Security
CareLab Health

Attachment: carelab_dpa_questions.pdf (summary)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@carelab.health>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-26T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence of non-training (CareLab production data) + subprocessor export path

Asha — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. We can absolutely produce an evidence bundle and an operational export map. Short plan below; full package attached.

Summary plan (high level):
- Non-training guarantee: Redwood will enforce a "no model improvement" flag for CareLab customer endpoints. Requests carrying that flag are segregated at the routing layer and are never written to long-term telemetry or model training stores. We will provide: (a) a signed ops runbook with play-by-play enforcement steps; (b) an export of access logs filtered to CareLab (timeboxed sample); (c) a KMS-backed key rotation statement showing encryption-at-rest for transient KV.
- Evidence pack: we attached no-train-evidence-pack_v1.pdf that contains screenshots of config, sample logs, and an audit checklist.
- Subprocessor export plan: included as a CSV (subprocessor_inventory.csv) plus a short narrative describing EU-onshore fallback routing and cross-region transfer controls.

Next steps we propose:
1) Kimberly (CC) to review DPA redline and confirm which clauses we can accept as-is vs need legal.
2) David (CC) to confirm ops-level artifacts we can share (sampling windows / redaction).
3) Priyom to deliver the evidence bundle to your procurement contact by end-of-week.

If that works, we will also include a short, signed statement from our Head of Security confirming the no-train policy specifically for CareLab.

Thanks — will follow up with attachments.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: no-train-evidence-pack_v1.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-27T08:37:00Z
Subject: Internal: quick read on CareLab DPA redline + evidence scope

Folks — I reviewed CareLab's redline (attached) and have three notes:

1) No-training clause: they want an express contract language that prohibits any derivative training on any internal models. Legal prefers to keep the provision scoped to "no model improvement" for customer-specific inputs processed under the flagged endpoint. We should accept that operational scope and provide the additional evidence package Asha requested.

2) Subprocessor transfers: procurement asked for a specific onshore fallback. Ops can commit to EU-onshore fallback (we use the EU dedicated pool for their tenant) but we need to confirm the cross-border transfer gating for telemetry used for debugging. David, can you confirm which telemetry we can mark ephemeral and avoid exporting? Also, is there an automated route that never crosses out of EU for that tenant?

3) Evidence artefacts: propose we include a signed one-page attestation, a 30-day sample of redactable logs, a screenshot of the routing config that shows EU-only routing, and our subprocessor inventory CSV (scrubbed).

I recommend we push the textual redline acceptance + bundle together so procurement has both legal and operational proof.

— Kim
Director, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-28T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: quick read on CareLab DPA redline + evidence scope

Kim / Priyom — quick confirmation from infra:

- For flagged endpoints (CareLab tenant flag), telemetry that is stored beyond ephemeral memory is only anonymized telemetry (tokenized session ids, request sizes, error traces) and is written to our EU-dedicated log cluster. No model training datasets are ever created from those logs.
- We can implement an additional export gating rule in the routing layer that prevents any log exports to non-EU destinations for tenants with the "EU resident" tag. We already have the EU-dedicated pool for Dedicated customers; for Hosted we can pin their routing policy to the EU cluster.
- I will prepare a 30-day sample of redacted logs (sensitive fields removed) and a short runbook showing the export gating rule. ETA: 2028-04-30 EOD.

Two operational caveats to call out:
1) If CareLab requests incident forensics that require controlled export outside EU, we'll require an explicit, timebound authorization (procurement/legal) and we will log that approval.
2) Our SRE debugging flow sometimes requires ephemeral traces to be sent to a US debugging sandbox; we can opt-out CareLab from that sandbox via the tenant tag.

I'll attach the log sample and runbook when ready.

— David
Head of Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessor_inventory.csv (redacted)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@carelab.health>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-30T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence of non-training (CareLab production data) + subprocessor export path

Asha — attaching the evidence bundle and the DPA redline as promised. Quick summary of what’s included:

- no-train-evidence-pack_v1.pdf: one-page signed attestation from Redwood Head of Security, ops runbook excerpt showing enforcement of the tenant-level "no model improvement" flag, screenshots of routing config pinned to EU pool, and a sampling of redacted logs (30 days).
- subprocessor_inventory.csv: scrubbed inventory showing EU-only analytics and onshore fallback pools.
- dpa_redline_CareLab_v3.docx: our proposed redline; we accepted the core no-training ask but kept the language scoped to requests processed under the CareLab tenant flag and excluded aggregated telemetry used for platform health (anonymized).

Operational notes:
- We will apply an EU-only export gating for CareLab by default. Any request to export for incident forensics must be a signed, timeboxed authorization from CareLab security and procurement; we will log and surface those approvals.
- We will complete the runbook + log sample upload to your shared Drive folder and provide a short walk-through (15–20 min) with your security team.

Please confirm if procurement needs anything else to close the order by 05/05. Happy to hop on a short call if you want us to walk through the evidence pack.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: no-train-evidence-pack_v1.pdf, subprocessor_inventory.csv, dpa_redline_CareLab_v3.docx
